_enforcement_note: block: refuse the tool call and explain. warn: allow but inject the reason as feedback. off: allow silently. The TB_COMMAND_POLICY env var overrides this value for one session, which is the documented rollback path -- edit this file for a durable change.

bounded_output._note: Project directive: fetch at most 30 lines per call, then request the next 30. A read command must carry an explicit bound (head -N, tail -N, sed -n 'a,bp', grep -m N, git log -n N, --max-count) with N <= max_declared_lines. When the bound is satisfied the output is returned normally; when it is not, the only thing that leaves the hook is refusal_message.
bounded_output._exempt_note: Commands whose output is either trivially small or whose own tooling already bounds it (pytest -q, ruff, git with -n). Exemption applies to the FIRST word of a pipeline segment only; a pipeline that ends in an unbounded reader is still checked.
bounded_output._subcommand_note: Commands that are exempt as a whole but have subcommands whose output is unbounded. `git` is exempt so that `git status` and `git add` are not nagged, but `git log` with no -n can page thousands of commits into context.
bounded_output._oversized_note: A bound that is present but large is not a bound. head -100 puts 100 lines in context just as surely as cat does. These patterns extract the declared N and compare it against max_declared_lines; sed ranges are compared by span.
bounded_output._byte_note: head -c is a legitimate bound for output with no newlines, but a byte bound is still a bound: -c 500000 is unbounded in practice. Compared against max_declared_bytes rather than max_declared_lines.
bounded_output._count_note: grep -c emits a single count line, so it is inherently bounded and must not be treated as an unbounded read just because it follows a reader in the pipeline.
bounded_output.refusal_message: only <=30 lines are allowed,run command for minimum line which can make you understand the failure
bounded_output._gh_note: `gh` is not exempt as a whole, but `gh run view --log`, `gh run list` and `gh api .../logs` page an entire CI run into context. They are allowed only behind an explicit bound; `gh pr view/checks/merge` are untouched.

destructive._note: Destructive commands are refused outright. They are not blocked because they are forbidden -- they are blocked because they must be run through common/shell_exec.run() with classification='destructive' and confirm_destructive=True, which records the authorization. The hook names that path in its refusal.
destructive._allow_marker_note: Prefixing a command with this marker documents that a human authorized this specific irreversible action. The marker is deliberately noisy so it cannot be added by habit.

secret_echo._note: Refuse commands that would print a credential store straight into the transcript, which is how a secret ends up in an LLM context and in the session log.

ci_observability._note: Permanent, not situational. CI live-monitoring -- following a run, watching checks, or a poll loop -- streams an unbounded and open-ended amount of build output into context, and no per-call line bound can cap something that never ends. Bulk log and report retrieval is capped by bounded_output instead: the minimum number of lines that explains the failure is always permitted.
ci_observability.message: CI live monitoring is permanently disabled. only <=30 lines are allowed,run command for minimum line which can make you understand the failure
ci_observability._banned_tools_note: The Monitor tool is a live watch by construction, so it is refused for this project regardless of what it is pointed at.
